scenarios.input: The plan is done. Implement milestone 1: add the retry loop to the uploader with its regression test. Answer in 6 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The prompt uses the documented trigger `implement this slice` in substance and follows a plan. A response that assigns a complexity tier, runs a pre-mortem before code, and writes the failing test before the implementation is attributable to this skill rather than to generic coding help.

scenarios.desc: A new detector must be self-applied before it is committed
scenarios.input: Add a pre-push linter that flags any function over 80 lines, plus a unit test for it against a fixture. The fixture test passes, so we are done. Answer in 6 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: This is the discriminating case. A fixture test proves the detector's logic and proves nothing about its threshold, so a generic responder accepts the claim of done. Step 6 requires running the new detector against the current branch and confirming it fires on conditions already present. A response that demands that run before the commit is attributable to the skill.

scenarios.desc: Reviewing a finished diff is not building
scenarios.input: Read the diff on this branch and tell me whether the architecture is sound. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: This asks for review of finished work, which the skill's description routes elsewhere. It names no slice, no plan step, and no implementation trigger, so build should stay inactive.
